summary: Validated private APK download reliability scope end-to-end: backend ticket/range contracts, helper browser flows (real downloads), timeout/retry behavior, and baseline hash integrity.
action_items: No blocking defects found in the requested private download reliability scope.
Upstream/proxy log redaction cannot be verified from this environment; only app-level uvicorn access log filter behavior was unit-tested.
critical_code_review_comments: Helper script now correctly targets /api/download/vesper-native-ticket for 404 and intercepted-request scenarios; old /vesper-native-apk expectation was stale.
Browser flow confirms no JS fetch/xhr for full APK endpoints during valid downloads (browser-managed download handoff path used).
Ticket log redaction filter masks only ticket-query targets and preserves non-ticket access log targets in unit checks.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Executed backend pytest file pair with JUnit output at /app/test_reports/pytest/iteration_128_native_download.xml; all passed. Browser helper run via /tmp/vesper-browser-check/bin/python produced 9 PASS at /app/test_reports/artifacts_iter128_download_browser/result.json including real APK save+hash checks before/after reload, manual direct-link click, timeout retry, stale response discard, and cross-origin ticket URL rejection checks. Frontend baseline hash checker returned baseline_entries=515, missing=0, mismatches=0.
rca of the issue: Primary historical reliability gap was helper behavior around delayed ticket preparation and stale client harness assumptions. Current implementation behavior validates: short ticket POST, browser-managed file transfer, 10s AbortController timeout with retry re-enable, and retained capability handling. Test-only simulations for timeout/network/storage/time are MOCKED within Playwright route/JS interception; actual APK transfer and integrity verification were real.
